consensus_expectations: Sell-side mean target price NOK 99.35 (17 analysts covering the OB:NHY target-price line; 12-15 analysts still contributing to the EPS/EBITDA/Revenue consensus lines), average recommendation Hold 2.94/5 [decision_record.json variant_perception_summary; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md SS1, citing NorskHydroASAOBNHYEstimatesReport.xls, Consensus tab, data as of 2026-07-15]. NOK 99.35 implies ~17% upside from the pool-verified price (NOK 84.96, 2026-07-17). FY2026 consensus: revenue NOK 213,365.5m, EBITDA NOK 36,330.5m, EPS Normalized NOK 8.80 (as of 2026-07-15). FQ2 2026 (due 2026-07-22) consensus was cut in the final 30 days before this run -- EBITDA -9.5%, EPS -5.5% at the FQ2 line -- while FQ2 revenue was still revised net-upward (3 up, 1 down) in the same window, and the 3-month revision breadth for FY2026 EBITDA/EPS/Revenue is still net positive following the FQ1 2026 beat. Read together: the Street's near-term profit numbers already track management's own guided Q2 cost bridge (higher energy/carbon/raw-material costs, lower Aluminium Metal volumes), but the mean 12-month price target (NOK 99.35) has evidently not been marked down by a comparable amount -- it sits well above not just the current price but also this run's own base case.
market_implied_expectations: Reverse-DCF (valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md), inverting the primary DCF's own WACC (7.50%), 5-year horizon and terminal g (2.5%) against the canonical EV (NOK 192,384mm): the primary solve implies a -3.21% 5-yr FCF CAGR off the FY2025 FCF base -- undemanding in isolation, but this reading is flagged as misleading because FY2025 FCF (NOK 11,729mm) was itself inflated by a favorable working-capital swing versus FY2024 (NOK 1,801mm). The more reliable secondary solve -- holding 04's own revenue/D&A/capex/NWC path fixed and solving for the single Adjusted EBITDA margin needed -- implies a uniform 14.02% margin (~9.0% EBIT margin) sustained FY2026-2030, about 90bps ABOVE the FY2025 actual (13.9%) and materially above the DCF's own 13.0% mid-cycle anchor and the FY2023 trough (11.5%). Verdict per the module: 'Stretch, tilting aggressive' -- the price does not require the Q1 2026 shock margin (17.2%) or the current ~17% sell-side FY2026-28 consensus margin to persist, but it does require today's elevated cycle position to hold durably above the DCF's own conservative anchor. WACC, not the FCF base or terminal g, is the dominant lever (an 8.3pp CAGR swing per +/-1% WACC vs a 5.7pp swing on the FCF-base band) because the DCF is terminal-value-dominated (78.1% of EV) -- so the 'what's priced in' read is really a joint bet on WACC staying near 7.5% AND the margin not fading to 13.0%.
engine_view: Weighted base-case fair value NOK 81.83/share (-3.7% vs price) -- a blend of sum-of-the-parts (40% weight, NOK 84.63, tied within 0.3% of the consolidated EV bridge on audited segment Adjusted EBITDA), intrinsic DCF (35% weight, NOK 70.14, terminal-dominated at 78.1% of EV, confidence capped at 60), and quality-adjusted peer-relative (25% weight, NOK 93.70, stacking a derived NOK/USD 9.63 FX conversion and a discretionary 10% quality discount on an imperfect 3-name core comp set) [valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md SS1, SS3]. Bull NOK 107.70 (+26.8%, 20% prob) / Base NOK 81.83 (-3.7%, 55% prob) / Bear NOK 45.12 (-46.9%, 25% prob, a structural not cyclical moat-erosion reset) [final_thesis.md SS8]. Probability-weighted expected return -8.4%, risk/reward -0.18, margin of safety -3.83%, downside to bear 46.89%. Decision: Watchlist -- but the binding cap on the headline is RF-OWN-004 (the Norwegian State's unaligned 34.3-34.5% stake), not the valuation read itself; even if the valuation gap were resolved bullishly, the governance cap holds the rating at Watchlist or lower.
what_everyone_knows: Norsk Hydro is a state-linked, vertically integrated aluminium producer whose earnings are dominated by the LME aluminium price and the USD/NOK rate, currently benefiting from a Middle East-driven supply-shock price spike that management itself calls non-repeatable.
what_is_priced_in: The current price (NOK 84.96) requires Hydro's elevated FY2025 actual Adjusted EBITDA margin (13.9%) to hold roughly flat through 2030 and into perpetuity, not to grow (implied 5-yr FCF CAGR -3.21%) -- about 90bps above the DCF's own 13.0% mid-cycle anchor. This is a real, evidenced 'Stretch, tilting aggressive' ask, not an undemanding one, per the reverse-DCF.
what_market_may_be_missing: The engine's stated candidates for a market blind spot are: (1) ~67% of Q2 2026 primary aluminium volume is already booked at USD 3,000/mt against a USD 3,467/mt quarter-end spot -- the company's own forward hedge book already shows partial, not full, reversion; (2) the FQ2 2026 EBITDA/EPS consensus was cut in the 30 days before this report specifically to track management's own guided cost bridge (higher energy/carbon/raw-material costs, lower volumes), not out of independent Street caution, while FQ2 revenue itself was still revised upward in the same window; (3) Hydro Extrusions' EBIT margin is already negative (-2.2%, FY2025) with no delivered turnaround evidence (plant closures proposed, not completed); (4) the Q1 2026 receivables build (DSO 33.0 to 56.7 days, AR +82.3% QoQ vs +6.7% revenue growth) is unexplained in the pool and untested by a second data point.
evidence_engine_is_different: The engine's own falsification test: if FQ2 2026 (22-Jul-2026, three days after this run) shows the Adjusted EBITDA margin falling back below ~15% while receivables normalize and CFO turns positive, the SOTP-anchored base case (NOK 81.83) is directionally vindicated over the sell-side's higher target; if the margin instead holds near 17%+ with clean cash conversion, the sell-side's more bullish read is confirmed and this synthesis was too conservative. Independent assessment: this is a genuine, checkable falsification trigger, but resolving it does NOT by itself prove the engine held a differentiated view before the print -- items (1)-(3) above are drawn from Hydro's own investor presentation (nhy-presentation-q1-2026.pdf, the Q2 outlook bridge slides) and audited segment disclosures, materials any of the 17 covering sell-side analysts already have, and the estimate-revision data in earnings/04 shows the Street's near-term EPS/EBITDA numbers had ALREADY been cut to track that same guided cost bridge before this report was written. That means the 'edge' is largely a bet that the sell-side's 12-month PRICE TARGET (built on a longer-horizon multiple/DCF view, methodology unknown from this pool) has not been updated as fast as its near-term estimate line, not a bet on facts the market lacks. Item (4), the receivables anomaly, is the one candidate with real informational novelty -- a forensic catch not surfaced in the earnings call or the guided bridge -- but the engine does not tie it quantitatively to the valuation gap; it supports the accounting-quality caution and the bear scenario, not the consensus-vs-engine price disagreement specifically.
base_rate_check: Per CLAUDE.md SS9, an exceptional forecast needs exceptional evidence. The bear case (-46.9%, 25% probability) is a large single-scenario move, but its MAGNITUDE is not obviously exceptional against the base rate for cyclical metals equities -- aluminium/commodity producer equities have historically moved 40-60% peak-to-trough within a single down-cycle (the balance-sheet-survival module's own stress test confirms the underlying business survives a 30-71% EBITDA decline with no covenant breach, i.e. the equity downside is a re-rating/multiple-compression story layered on a real but survivable earnings decline, not a solvency event). What IS exceptional is the bear case's causal LABEL -- 'structural, not cyclical' moat erosion -- when the supporting evidence is narrower than the label: one segment (Extrusions, EBIT margin -2.2%, no delivered turnaround) plus a general, not-yet-realized risk (Chinese/Gulf capacity growth pressuring the upstream cost curve). The upstream Aluminium Metal segment -- 58.7% of gross EV and the segment carrying the primary cost-curve advantage -- has NOT shown a structural break in this run's evidence; its margin decline so far is consistent with ordinary cyclical price normalization (the reverse-DCF's own reconciliation). Labeling a still-mostly-cyclical reversion as 'structural' asks for more evidentiary weight than a single underperforming, smaller segment provides. Net: the -46.9% magnitude is within the ordinary base rate for a commodity-cyclical bear case; the 'structural' framing attached to it is the part that outruns the evidence on hand.
gap_direction: Fairly priced on the engine's own point estimate, tilting slightly overvalued (-3.7%, engine base fair value NOK 81.83 vs price NOK 84.96) -- but this label is not robust to method choice: the three weighted valuation methods that feed that -3.7% blend individually range from -17.4% (intrinsic DCF, NOK 70.14 -- says overvalued) to +10.2% (peer-relative, NOK 93.70 -- says undervalued), with SOTP roughly at fair value (-0.4%, NOK 84.63). Separately, the engine's own base case sits -17.6% BELOW the sell-side consensus mean target (NOK 81.83 vs NOK 99.35) -- a materially more bearish read than the market's own forward-looking price target, even though the engine's near-term operating read (margin fading toward 13.0%) is not dramatically different from what the Street's own recent estimate cuts already imply.
notes: Do not read edge_score/is_exploitable as contradicting the run's Watchlist call -- they are answering a narrower question (is there a genuine, differentiated informational edge behind the valuation gap) and the answer is largely no: three of the four 'what the market may be missing' points are drawn from Hydro's own public investor-presentation bridge and audited segment disclosures already available to all 17 covering analysts, and the estimate-revision data shows the Street's near-term numbers already track that same guidance. The one item with genuine novelty (the Q1 2026 receivables/DSO spike) is real but tangential to the consensus-vs-engine valuation disagreement and is better read as an earnings-quality flag (already captured in the run's accounting-quality compound red flag) than as the source of a pricing edge. Two other axes are worth carrying forward for whoever reviews this: (a) the -3.7% headline gap sits well inside a 33.6% cross-method dispersion band, so 'modestly overvalued' and 'modestly undervalued' are both defensible reads depending on method weighting -- the SOTP method (most trusted, audited-data-anchored) alone puts the stock almost exactly at fair value (-0.4%); (b) the real decision driver in this run is not the valuation gap at all but the RF-OWN-004 governance cap (unaligned Norwegian State owner), which holds the rating at Watchlist regardless of how the valuation-gap question above resolves -- closing the valuation gap would not, by itself, change the recommended action. Independent read is somewhat more skeptical than the engine's own self-graded edge_score of 30/100; this review puts it at 25/100 for the reasons above, still well below the 50-point 'proven edge' bar either way.
